Tasks: what you will do

Peec ships something new almost every week. Most customers hear about it late, and some never do. We're hiring a Customer Education Manager to own how customers learn Peec. You'll own the product docs, the changelog, product updates and in-app communication, and turn every release into something a busy marketer understands in a minute.

You'll sit in product marketing and report to our founding product marketer. You'll work every day with product managers and engineers to understand what's shipping, with customer success to see where customers get stuck, and with the growth team to see what actually changes how people use the product.

What you'll do

• Own the product docs. Rebuild them around the jobs customers come to do, not around the menu. Keep them current with every release, and make them easy to read for people and for the AI assistants our customers now ask first.

• Run the changelog and product updates. Every release gets a clear entry the day it ships. You write the regular product update and the announcement for bigger launches, and decide what deserves which.

• Write in-app communication. You write the copy for announcements, tooltips, empty states, onboarding steps and feature nudges. The growth team runs the nudges themselves (who sees what, when, and the tests); you make sure every message is clear, accurate and sounds like one product.

• Make product content that teaches. Short how-to videos, walkthroughs, use-case guides and templates that get a new user from signup to their first useful insight, and an existing customer to the feature they're missing.

• Get in early. Sit with product and engineering before launch, early enough to shape naming, setup and the first-run experience, not just document them afterwards.

• Fix questions at the source. Read support tickets and customer calls, find the questions we keep answering, and make sure the product, docs or messaging answer them before anyone has to ask.

title: Design Engineer (w/m/d)
description:
Heartworking in Hannover. In Voll- oder Teilzeit. Hybrid.

Wir suchen jemanden, der/die Interfaces gestaltet und baut – und Verantwortung für das Produkt übernimmt, bis es im Browser genauso gut funktioniert wie in der Vorstellung. Tarifrechner, Kundenportale, Antragsflows, Konfiguratoren, Websites – Anwendungen, bei denen hunderttausende Menschen nicht merken sollen, wie komplex "das unter der Haube" ist. Die WordPress-Landingpage von der Stange gibt's woanders.

Aufgaben

So sieht dein Alltag aus

• Du entwirfst und baust Interfaces – vom Konzept über den visuellen Entwurf bis in den funktionierenden Code. Du kannst ein Feature von der Idee bis in den Browser bringen, ohne es abgeben zu müssen. Das heißt nicht, dass du alles alleine machst – im Team arbeiten Entwickler:innen mit dir im selben Codebase. Aber du bist nicht abhängig davon, dass jemand anderes deinen Entwurf interpretiert.

• Du arbeitest mit modernen Tools, die die Grenze zwischen Design und Code auflösen – Nordcraft, Cursor, v0 und was sonst in der Praxis taugt. Genauso selbstverständlich schreibst du eigenen Code, wenn das die bessere Lösung ist. Du evaluierst neue Ansätze mit Neugier, aber ohne Hype: nicht jedes Tool, das in der Community trendet, verdient deine Zeit.

• Du baust und pflegst Design-Systeme dort, wo sie hingehören: im Code. Tokens, Komponenten, Varianten, Dokumentation – als lebendiges System, das direkt im Produkt funktioniert.

• Du sitzt mit den Entwickler:innen zusammen – wirklich, nicht bildlich. Ihr arbeitet im selben Codebase, reviewed euch gegenseitig, diskutiert Architektur und Umsetzung auf Augenhöhe.

• Du arbeitest in interdisziplinären Kundenteams (ca. 4–8 Personen aus Beratung, PM, Design und Development) – direkt am Kunden. Du bist nicht nur für deinen Teil zuständig, sondern denkst über den gesamten Produktkontext mit. Auch nach dem Go-Live.

• Du denkst in messbarer Wirkung: Analytics, Heatmaps, Conversion-Daten – du nutzt sie, um deine Designentscheidungen zu validieren und das Produkt kontinuierlich besser zu machen.

• Du machst andere besser: Design-Reviews, Code-Reviews, ehrliches Feedback, Wissenstransfer. Du bewegst dich zwischen Design- und Dev-Welt und bringst beide Seiten näher zusammen – durch gemeinsame Sprache, nicht nur durch Tools.

• AI ist für dich Werkzeug im Alltag. Du nutzt Cursor für Code-Generierung, v0 für schnelle UI-Exploration, Claude oder ChatGPT für Prototyping und Konzeptvalidierung. Und du weißt, dass gute AI-Ergebnisse davon abhängen, wie präzise du den Kontext definierst: Design-System-Regeln, technische Constraints, Markensprache. Sauber denken, bevor du loslegst.

Qualifikation

Das bringst du mit

• Mehrjährige Erfahrung an der Schnittstelle von Design und Frontend-Entwicklung. Du kommst entweder aus dem Design und hast dir Code beigebracht, oder aus der Entwicklung und hast ein starkes Gespür für Gestaltung entwickelt. Beides ist willkommen.

• Du kannst Interfaces entwerfen UND bauen: HTML, CSS/SCSS, JavaScript/TypeScript. Du fühlst dich in Figma genauso wohl wie in VS Code oder Cursor.

• Konzeptionelles Denken: Du verstehst, wie Informationsarchitekturen und User Flows funktionieren, und kannst diese in deinen Entwürfen und deinem Code gleichermaßen abbilden.

• Du arbeitest sicher mit modernen Frontend-Technologien – React/Next.js bevorzugt, aber wenn du aus einem anderen Ökosystem kommst und schnell lernst: gerne. Erfahrung mit Nordcraft oder vergleichbaren visuellen Development-Plattformen ist ein Plus.

• Design-Systeme lebst du im Code: Tokens, Komponenten, Varianten – aufbauen, dokumentieren, weiterentwickeln.

• Visuelles Gespür: Typografie, Farbe, Spacing, Responsive Design, Animationen – du erkennst, wenn etwas nicht stimmt, und du kannst es selbst fixen. Accessibility (WCAG) gehört für dich zur Grundhaltung.

• Kommunikation: Du kannst Designentscheidungen gegenüber dem Team und Kunden argumentieren. Und du sprichst die Sprache beider Seiten – du erklärst Entwickler:innen, warum ein Detail wichtig ist, und Designer:innen, warum eine technische Einschränkung kein Kompromiss sein muss.

• Du hast echte Erfahrung mit AI-Tools im Arbeitsalltag – nicht als Experiment, sondern als festen Teil deines Workflows. Du weißt, wo sie echten Mehrwert bringen und wo du besser selbst baust. Und du verstehst, dass die Qualität der Ergebnisse von der Qualität deines Denkens abhängt – nicht vom Tool.

• Du kannst dich in komplexe Fachlichkeiten einarbeiten und bleibst auch bei langfristigen Kundenbeziehungen neugierig, statt auf Autopilot zu schalten.

• Deutsch auf C1-Niveau – unsere Kunden und Workshops sind deutschsprachig. Englisch im Code und in der Dokumentation ist selbstverständlich

Du entsprichst nicht zu 100% allen Anforderungen, aber die Chemie stimmt? Kein Problem! Richtig Bock auf Digitales ist uns wichtiger als ein shiny Lebenslauf.

Benefits

Darauf kannst du dich bei uns freuen

• Gehalt: Wir zahlen marktgerecht und transparent – den konkreten Gehaltsrahmen besprechen wir offen im Erstgespräch. Kein Pokern, kein Rätselraten.

• Gelebte Work-Life-Integration. Viele von uns haben Familie oder zeitintensive Hobbys. Wir sind überzeugt, dass nachhaltige Ausgeglichenheit uns viel weiter bringt als Mitarbeiter:innen mehr Zeit abzuverlangen.

• Hybrides Arbeiten: 3 Tage remote, 2 Tage gemeinsam vor Ort am Hanomaghof. Nicht wegen Kontrolle, sondern weil wir glauben, dass echte Kreativität vom Austausch in einem Raum lebt – vom Miteinander zwischen Menschen, das kein Call ersetzen kann. Jeden zweiten Dienstag: Agentur-Standup und gemeinsames (veganes) Mittagessen mit Catering.

• Das, was andere nur „flache Hierarchien" nennen – und wir tatsächlich meinen: Dein Team Lead hat immer eine offene Tür, du sprichst direkt mit Kunden statt über drei Ecken, und wenn du eine Idee hast, brauchst du kein Ticket dafür.

• Fort- und Weiterbildung ohne Deckel: Konferenzen, Kurse, Bücher, Zertifizierungen – du suchst aus, wir zahlen.

• Moderne Tools: GitHub, Linear, Slack, Figma. Und ja, wir setzen AI-Tools im Arbeitsalltag ein – kein Verbot, kein Hype, sondern pragmatischer Einsatz.

• Mitdenken und Mitgestalten. Du hast von Anfang an die Möglichkeit, Verantwortung zu übernehmen und Dinge zu verändern.

• Ob macOS oder Linux – du suchst dir deine Hard- und Software selbst aus. Auch für den privaten Gebrauch.

• Mobilität: Deutschlandticket (geht auf uns) und Jobrad-Leasing.

• Und sonst: Siebträger-Espresso, frisches Obst, Softdrinks, betriebliche Altersvorsorge, VWL, Sommerfest, Weihnachtsfeier, Teamevents und Agentur-Offsite.

Dein Weg zu uns

• Bewirb dich mit deinem Lebenslauf und optional einem Portfolio, Case Studies oder Arbeitsproben. Kein Anschreiben nötig.

• Unser erstes Kennenlerngespräch geht auch per Video – aber persönlich ist netter, und unser Kaffee ist wirklich sehr gut. ☕ Mit dabei: Du, jemand aus dem Design-Team und Jan-Christoph (Geschäftsführer).

• It's a match? Beim Kennenlerntag lernst du das Team, die Projekte und den Hanomaghof kennen. Gemeinsames Mittagessen, offene Fragen, echtes Beschnuppern.

• Ein „JA!" von allen Beteiligten? Dann schicken wir dir den Entwurf für deinen Arbeitsvertrag rüber und besprechen alle Details.

• Ab Tag 1: persönliches Onboarding mit fachlicher Einarbeitung, Buddy-System und regelmäßigem Feedback durch die ersten Monate. 🥳

title: Warehouse Specialist
description:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION

• You will get to work on some of the most complex tech challenges to bring abundant, safe, clean energy to the world.

• You'll get to join and learn from an exceptional selection of accomplished and driven individuals.

• Do your life’s best work and enjoy the journey.

• Get to show that big things are possible in Europe when you assemble the best talent.

YOUR IMPACT

At Proxima Fusion, we are building the future of clean energy - and we need an experienced Warehouse Specialist who thrives in a fast-paced, hands-on environment. In this role, you will ensure the smooth and efficient flow of materials and equipment, supporting our engineering, R&D, and operational ambitions. You’ll be responsible for managing incoming and outgoing goods, maintaining accurate inventory records, coordinating shipments, and ensuring the safe handling and storage of materials. With a strong focus on reliability, precision, and continuous improvement, you’ll play a key role in building efficient and scalable warehouse operations that support our mission to make fusion energy a reality.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

• Goods receipt and inspection: Receive deliveries from suppliers, carriers and couriers. Check each one against the purchase order and delivery note for quantity, part number and condition. Look for transport damage, moisture, contamination or tampering. Verify labels, batch and serial numbers, and shelf life.

• Non-conformance and claims: Photograph and document any findings. Move non-conforming goods to blocked or quarantine stock and raise non-conformance reports. File claims with carriers, inform Purchasing, and hand parts that need detailed inspection to Quality. Release or return them based on Quality’s decision.

• System accuracy (ERP/WMS): Post goods receipts and goods issues accurately and on time, including labels, barcodes, and batch and serial numbers. Book goods in only after they pass the receipt checks. Keep physical stock and system stock in sync.

• Dispatch and shipping documents: Pick, pack and prepare shipments according to packing instructions. Create delivery notes, labels, CMR consignment notes and packing lists. For non-EU shipments, prepare proforma invoices and export documents with the logistics team. Prepare ADR transport documents for hazardous goods.

• Carrier coordination and returns: Book and coordinate pickups, and track shipments until they’re delivered. Handle returns and re-shipments to suppliers through the RMA process.

• Loading, unloading and transport: Load and unload trucks and vans safely with forklifts and pallet jacks, and secure loads correctly. Handle heavy, bulky, sensitive or high-value components with care. Run scheduled milk runs between company sites and local suppliers using company vehicles.

• Storage, replenishment and inventory: Sort, label and store goods in the correct locations. Replenish production and line-side stock (Kanban or min/max) in time for manufacturing. Take part in the annual stocktake and resolve stock differences. Manage packaging materials: stock levels, reordering, reuse and recycling.

• Housekeeping and safety: Keep receiving, storage and dispatch areas clean and organised with a 5S mindset. Separate and dispose of waste according to German recycling rules. Follow health and safety rules and wear PPE. Report hazards, near-misses and accidents, and carry out daily checks on forklifts and handling equipment.

• Cross-functional coordination: Work with Purchasing, Production, Quality, Engineering and Finance on material availability, priorities and urgent shipments, and keep internal customers informed.

• Continuous improvement and travel: Suggest and support improvements to warehouse processes, layout and digital tools. Travel within the EU when needed, for example to suppliers, partner sites or with special shipments.

WHO YOU ARE

• Completed vocational training as Fachkraft für Lagerlogistik, Fachlagerist/in or a comparable qualification, or equivalent hands-on experience.

• At least 5 years of experience in goods receipt, dispatch or warehousing, ideally in a manufacturing environment.

• Valid EU/German driving licence, class B.

• Valid forklift licence (Staplerschein per DGUV Grundsatz 308-001) and confident operation of counterbalance forklifts.

• Fluent German and English, spoken and written (at least B2 in both).

• Tech-savvy: confident with ERP/WMS systems (e.g. SAP or similar), barcode scanners, Google Workspace, and email.

• Good knowledge of shipping documents and processes (delivery notes, CMR, Incoterms basics).

• Knowledge of load securing and safe handling of goods.

• Willingness to travel within the EU when required.

INTERVIEW PROCESS

Every step of the way, you will have the opportunity to influence our direction. Through our platforms, we create engaging, safe, and thoughtfully designed learning experiences that help children grow academically, creatively, and personally. Every feature we ship, every system we scale, and every improvement we make contributes to shaping how the next generation learns and discovers their potential. If our platform is down, a child might not go to school that day. We’re looking for leaders who want their work to matter in classrooms and homes, who care about access to quality education, and who are excited to craft technology that makes a difference in young people’s lives. Here, your impact doesn’t just power a product; it shapes future generations!

What you’ll work on

We’re a C# and Vue.js platform growing towards a scale that no longer matches our legacy architecture. You’ll need to work with your team balancing both product and engineering initiatives. You’ll report to our head of engineering and be expected to split your time roughly 50/50 between people management and hands-on development. Prioritization always goes to leading and supporting your engineers.

How management works at Miaplaza

We're a US-based company, so this may differ from what you've done before:

• You start as an engineer. You’ll onboard as a senior engineer on your own team for two months, begin manager onboarding in month two, and take over the team at around week 10. Both phases matter equally, and this isn’t negotiable.

• You stay hands-on. Around 50% of your time stays hands-on after onboarding, but leading and supporting your engineers always comes first.

• You teach. Growing your engineers and those around you is a core responsibility. You'll have full oversight of your direct reports' work, because you can't teach well without seeing the process behind the output.

• Feedback is the norm. You'll give specific reinforcement and constructive feedback whenever you notice something, and you'll receive it too.

What you must bring

We can only move forward with candidates who meet these requirements:

• 7+ years of experience in software development in one or more object-oriented programming languages

• 3+ years of experience with front-end software development in a reactive front-end framework

• 3+ years of experience with software architecture

• 3+ years of experience operating at a Senior, Staff, or Principal Engineer level

• 2+ years of experience being a mentor/leader

• 1+ years leading a team, formally or as a tech lead

• Experience working directly with product and design on scoping and prioritization

• Experience being on-call and resolving production incidents

• A bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience

What makes you stand out

• Experience leading a team through a significant architectural migration

• Experience with consumer platforms at scale

• Experience building in regulated environments

• Experience with DevOps technologies (eg K8s, IaC, sysadmin, build pipelines, etc.)

• Extensive senior front-end development experience

Responsibilities

• Work with your teams to design, develop, and maintain scalable and reliable web applications using primarily C# and Vue.js

• Collaborate with your product trio (PM, UX, EM), product leadership team, and other EMs to scope, prioritize, and deliver features that matter to students and families

• Set the quality bar for your team. You'll have dedicated capacity for reliability and architecture work rather than fitting it around feature delivery, and a strong say in where that capacity goes.

• Manage, lead, and mentor your team while working side by side with them in code quality, clean architecture, soft skills, best practices, etc

• Lead team trainings, set SMART goals, hold performance reviews, and provide individual feedback recurrently to each of your devs

Our hiring process

As a remote company, we receive a large number of applicants, so our process is longer than usual. At every stage we try to respect your time.

• Application and CV review. We review your application answers and CV, then follow up with an update.

• Initial technical screen (20 min). A few administrative questions and short technical questions related to the role.

• Behavioral interview (1 hour). With a member of our HR team, about your experience and approach so far.

• 1st technical interview (1 hour). With a member of the engineering team to answer technical questions tailored to our work.

• 2nd technical interview (1 hour). With a member of the engineering team to dive into a hypothetical scenario and how you’d tackle it.

• Leadership interview (1 hour). With our Head of Engineering or executive leadership.

• Reference check. We contact the 3 references you provide, including at least one former or current manager, a colleague, and a former or current direct report.

• Offer and background check. Once you sign your offer, we run a background check in accordance with applicable law.

We give honest, timely feedback at every step. Job searches are hard; we don't want to make yours harder.

Compensation

The pay range for this role is €82,000 - 140,000. Our compensation philosophy aims for equity and competitiveness while considering regional differences in labor costs. Placement in the range depends on demonstrated skills, internal equity and local labor market rates for your area.

Miaplaza is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds. If you need accommodations at any point in the process, just let us know.

•

title: Senior Product Engineer
description:
Senior Product Engineer

Can you help us fix the world's most broken supply chain?

The fashion industry produces over 100 billion garments a year. 60% end up in landfill, not because people don't want these clothes, but because the supply chain for getting secondhand fashion from donation to resale is completely offline, manual, and broken.

Fleek is fixing this. Our mission is to make secondhand the first choice. We're building the infrastructure powering the global secondhand clothing trade, through a B2B marketplace and the AI systems digitising the supply chain behind it.

Through Fleek, vintage stores, online resellers, and retail buyers source graded secondhand inventory directly from wholesalers and rag houses across multiple countries. Our key enabler is FleekSort, an AI model fine-tuned on secondhand fashion, that can grade, price, and categorise items with just a photo, turning what has historically been an opaque and manual trade into a structured, searchable, and tradable global inventory layer.

Since 2022, we've saved 9 million items from landfill while tripling in size year-on-year. We're backed by some of the world's best investors, including a16z, Y Combinator, and HV Capital, alongside world-class angels who helped build Depop, Shopify, and Postmates.

Today, we serve thousands of resellers and retailers across the UK, Europe, and the US. With the secondhand fashion market projected to reach $350B by 2027, Fleek is building the AI-native operational and financial backbone for secondhand commerce globally.

We're looking for people who want to build something that matters, and move fast doing it. Sound good? Keep reading.

About the Role

This is a Senior Product Engineer role in Fleek's product engineering team, working across the stack. You'll report into our CTO, Sanket Agarwal (ex-Google, Postmates), and work embedded with a product manager and designer in a small, senior squad focused on the core marketplace experience.

Why This Role Stands Out

Fleek is digitising an industry that has never had technology. There are no existing playbooks for building an ecommerce experience around secondhand fashion at wholesale scale, where every item is unique, inventory is unpredictable, quality is graded by AI, and the supply chain spans three continents. You will be designing how the transaction layer works for a market that hasn't existed before.

You will be on our Growth team, owning the ecommerce journey from discovery to checkout, payment and credit systems, order management, and seller tools. Your systems will handle 500,000+ items a month today and million+ by the end of the year.

AI is at the core of everything we do, so you'll work closely with our data and AI teams to build the product features and services that connect FleekSort's classification engine to the marketplace experience.

We're looking for a product engineer who can think about how systems affect buyers and sellers at scale. You'll be expected to understand the business problems your code solves, and challenge whether we're solving the right ones.

What Makes You a Fleek Product Engineer?

• Product-Obsessed Builder: You think about what the seller sees when their inventory goes live, or why a buyer drops off at checkout. You instinctively connect technical decisions to commercial outcomes.

• Comfortable with Ambiguity: We're building systems for workflows that didn't exist before Fleek. You thrive when the problem is undefined and collaboration is key.

• Customer-Focused Thinker: You understand the dynamics of customer platforms and can understand how technical choices affect customers and our broader marketplace.

• Owner, Not Renter: You take a feature from problem definition to production and monitor it afterwards.

• Startup Pace: You've worked in environments where shipping matters more than perfection, where you deploy daily, and where velocity is a competitive advantage.

What You'll Do

• Own the Ecommerce Journey: Design and build the features and systems powering Fleek's core marketplace, across frontend and backend, from item discovery and search through to checkout, payment, and post-purchase. These are product features that directly drive GMV.

• Integrate AI into the Product: Build the features and services that connect FleekSort's AI classification engine to the marketplace experience, ensuring grading, pricing, and categorisation flow seamlessly into listings, search, and buyer workflows.

• Design for Scale: Architect systems that handle 500K+ items per month today, with a clear path to millions. Make pragmatic trade-offs between speed of delivery and long-term scalability.

• Shape Technical Direction: Contribute to architectural decisions across the stack. Challenge assumptions, propose alternatives, and help define engineering standards for a fast-growing team.

• Mentor and Elevate: Support the growth of more junior engineers through code reviews, pairing, and knowledge sharing. Help raise the technical bar across the team.

• Collaborate Cross-Functionally: Work embedded with your product manager and designer to define what gets built. Partner with data, AI, and operations teams to turn complex real-world logistics into reliable, scalable software.

What You Bring

• A track record of shipping product: You've built and owned user-facing features end to end, at a marketplace, fintech or consumer company; we care more about what you've shipped than how many years it took.

• You start from the user: You talk to buyers and sellers, watch where they get stuck, and can explain why what you're building matters to the person using it.

• You think like a PM: You shape the problem as well as the solution, push back when something doesn't feel right, and tie your work to GMV, conversion or retention.

• You ship fast and learn: You'd rather put a working version in front of users this week than a perfect one next quarter, and you're used to deploying daily.

• You measure what you build: You define success before you start and use data, user feedback and experiments to decide what to build next.

• You build AI-native: You use AI tools every day to move faster, and you've shipped features on LLMs or ML models, with evals to know they work.

• You work across the stack: You're strong in TypeScript and Node.js and comfortable enough on the frontend and in the data layer to ship a feature end to end, whichever way you lean.

• You have sound judgement: You make sensible trade-offs between speed and scale, think about failure modes in systems that move real money, and know when good enough is good enough.

Nice to Have

• Experience with marketplace dynamics: two-sided platforms, pricing, trust, supply-demand matching

• Familiarity with international systems and distributed teams across multiple time zones

A genuine excitement for building something from scratch in a category that didn't exist three years ago.

This Role Isn't for You If You Want:

• Narrow, siloed ownership where you only touch one service and never see the user

• Detailed specs handed to you before you start, we define problems together

• A slow-moving, highly structured environment with long release cycles

• Fully remote work, this team is on-site in London 3-4 days per week

• Pure infrastructure or platform work with no product exposure

Ready to build the infrastructure for the world's fastest-growing fashion economy? If you want to work on genuinely hard problems, with a world-class team, at a company that's tripling annually, we'd love to hear from you.

The Practicalities

• Location: London HQ, Commercial St, E1 (Liverpool St / Aldgate East)

• Work model: On-site

• Stage: Post-Series B, hyper-growth

• Team: 100+ across London, India, and Pakistan

• Stack: TypeScript and Node.js across frontend and backend, AI/ML integration

• Culture: High ownership, non-hierarchical, fast-moving. Founder-led with strong opinions loosely held.

What's In It for You?

Fleek is building the AI-native operational and financial backbone for a $350 billion market that has never been digitised. Joining now means you'll be part of the team that defines how the secondhand economy works, at scale, globally.

Why people join Fleek

• The problem is real: 9 million items saved from landfill since 2022. Your work has tangible, measurable impact.

• The AI is genuinely novel: FleekSort is an AI model fine-tuned on secondhand fashion, turning an opaque manual trade into a structured global inventory layer. This isn't a GPT wrapper.

• The growth is exceptional: Tripling year-on-year, ~$50M raised, Series B closed. Backed by a16z, Y Combinator, HV Capital, with advisors from Depop, Shopify, and Postmates.

• The timing is perfect: The secondhand market is projected to reach $350B by 2027. EU regulation is mandating the infrastructure Fleek builds. You're catching a wave.

• You'll have real ownership: 100-person company, no bureaucracy. You'll shape decisions and see the impact of your work immediately.

Our Values

Five values shape how we work at Fleek:

• Dream Big and Disrupt Yourself: Push the most ambitious version of what you're building. Step out of your comfort zone. Nothing is out of reach.

• Absolute Ownership: The buck stops with you. Drive initiatives to completion. Experiment, learn, persevere. The job isn't done until the job is done.

• Curiosity Leads the Way: Don't accept anything at face value. Ask questions you don't know the answer to. That's how you innovate.

• Talk to the Customer: Deeply understand their challenges, motivations, and ambitions. Every decision starts with the customer at the centre.

• Embrace Diversity: A global team building for a global supply chain. Bring your authentic self and embrace the diversity of everyone you encounter.

description:

Exa is an applied AI research lab organizing the entire web for AI. Agents don't search like people do. They ask long, complex questions and need clean, accurate, real-time answers. So we train our own retrieval models and index hundreds of billions of webpages, giving agents grounded, cited answers instead of stale training data.

And it's working. We've grown about 10x a year for three years, to more than $100M in annualized revenue and 2B+ requests a month from 200K+ teams. HubSpot, monday.com, Revolut, Firefox, Cognition, Cursor and OpenRouter all build on Exa. If you want to build core technology that's used every day, help build a generational company, and shape the revenue engine behind it, come join us.

About the role

Exa is hiring a Senior Field Operations Manager for EMEA, based in our new London office, to be the go-to partner for our EMEA sales leader, AEs, SDRs, partners and field engineers as the region grows from a handful of people into a full team.

You’ll bring our GTM operations and programs to EMEA, partnering with our Head of Revenue Programs to decide what we keep, what we localize and what we build new for the region’s markets.

You’ll be a swiss army knife across process, change management, light deal desk, insights and tools, with the relationships and judgment to tie it all together.

If you’ve helped build ops in a new region and you love being close to the field, we’d love to talk!

You'll lean hard on AI across all of this. We expect AI to do much of the reporting, drafting and checking, so your time goes to the field and the conversations only a person can have.

• Be the person our EMEA sales leader and team go to first. Listen for what matters to them, flag it, help them prioritize, and turn their problems into programs that stick.

• Stay really close to our EMEA AEs, SDRs, partners and field engineers. Know what’s working and what’s not, and work with our Insights team to spot patterns early, before they show up in the numbers.

• Roll out every change in EMEA, localized for our markets. Think through what each change will affect, and give each one a clear why, a playbook, training and a check-in on whether it stuck.

• Run EMEA’s operating rhythm: weekly pipeline and forecast reviews, QBR-style reviews and planning inputs, with decisions and follow-ups tracked.

• Help EMEA deals move through pricing, quoting and approvals with our US deal desk, Finance and Legal, including EMEA specifics like VAT, GDPR and local entities.

• Take our operations and programs from launch to running smoothly in EMEA, and adapt them to the region’s markets, languages and buying norms.

• Partner with our AMER Field Ops Manager on SDR process, and make it work for our EMEA SDR team.

• Get sellers up to speed on our tools and how each one fits into how we work with buyers, and help each seller set up a day that works for them.

• You’ve supported EMEA sellers and know how buying, contracting and selling differ across markets like UK and Ireland, DACH, France, the Nordics and Benelux.

• You’re a builder and a doer who loves to optimize and organize. You’ve built processes and programs your team actually used, kept them running, and made them better.

• You see how the whole GTM machine fits together, including where sales and field engineering meet. You think through the downstream impact of a change before it ships.

The Role

You will own the research question at the centre of LEA, our foundation model of the physical world: can a model learn what normally happens on a site, by place, hour and weather, so that an anomaly is simply what it did not expect? The first version is a probabilistic memory of each site. The next is a world model across every site that predicts the next state in latent space, starting from open world-model weights and growing on field data nobody else holds.

Our robots and cameras run on live security sites around the clock, and every event is kept with its clip, the model's verdict and the operator's outcome. That record is your dataset. You will work alongside our perception and model engineers, and your results go into production, not only into papers.

What You'll Work On

• Site memory: a learned, probabilistic model of each site: which people, vehicles and robots are where, at what hour, in what weather, and how the scene usually unfolds.

• Anomaly as surprise: replace rule-based alerting with measured surprise, and work out how to evaluate it when real incidents are rare.

• World model: post-train open world-model weights on aligned multi-sensor field sequences, JEPA-style, predicting in latent space rather than pixels.

• Transfer: from one site's memory to a model of all of them, and representations that carry across sites and domains.

• Research direction: choose the questions, design the experiments, and decide what is true before it ships.

title: Software Engineer, Robot Autonomy (Reliability & Test Infrastructure)
description:
Our Mission

At Laelaps AI, we believe robotics is entering a transformative decade, much like the arrival of the internet. Advances in AI, cloud computing, and hardware are reshaping what autonomous systems can do. Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient.

We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today!

The Role

You will own the path a code change takes from commit to robot, and the evidence behind every gate on that path. Today the honest answer to "is this build safe?" is "it worked on the test robot." You will replace that with a system: the simulation environment the team tests against, the regression suites that run on every change, the hardware-in-the-loop rigs, and the release gates that decide whether a build can go onto a robot that will patrol a customer site alone tonight.

This is the first engineer dedicated to reliability and test infrastructure, and it sits in our Robot Autonomy team, next to the engineers building perception, localisation, planning and locomotion. Our robots patrol security sites, critical infrastructure and defence facilities without a human present, so a bad release is not a rollback: it is a customer incident. Within six months, nothing should reach a customer robot without passing something you built.

What You'll Work On

• Release pipeline: code change, automated tests, simulation at scale, staging robot, pilot site, full rollout, with explicit pass criteria at every gate and nothing advancing without meeting them.

• Simulation as infrastructure: a GPU-backed simulation environment (Isaac Sim today) running continuously, so engineers test against scenarios instead of queueing for the one robot in the lab.

• Scenario libraries and regression suites: coverage across the whole on-robot stack, perception through locomotion, and the infrastructure to run thousands of scenarios on every change.

• Hardware-in-the-loop: bench rigs and test procedures on the physical robots for what simulation cannot tell you.

• Failure injection: drop sensors, degrade LiDAR returns, kill the network link, corrupt odometry, then verify the system degrades and recovers the way we tell customers it does.

• Field incidents to tests: when a robot misbehaves on site, reproduce it deterministically and turn it into a permanent regression test.

• Reproducibility: log capture, replay tooling, deterministic seeds, versioned scenarios, and coverage metrics that are honest about what they do not cover.

• Acceptance criteria: turn product and customer requirements into measurable tests, and report against them without softening the numbers.

Who We're Looking For

A test, validation or reliability engineer who has shipped a product where failure had consequences, and who has seen what changes when a fleet goes from one unit to fifty. You treat simulation and CI as production infrastructure that you own, not tools you consume. You have judgment about what is worth testing: we want a safety net, not a wall of green ticks that hides the real risk. And you are comfortable being the person who says a build is not going out.

Your Background

• 4+ years in test, validation, reliability, SRE or platform engineering on a product that shipped to customers.

• Experience with a complex system at scale: autonomous driving, drones, industrial automation, medical devices or similar.

• Strong Python and/or C++, with solid CI/CD and containerised infrastructure skills.

• Hands-on with a robotics simulator run as production infrastructure: Isaac Sim preferred, Gazebo, MuJoCo or equivalent accepted.

• Comfortable owning cloud infrastructure and GPU orchestration, not just consuming it.

• Enough hardware literacy to read a timing problem or a flaky sensor trace, and the judgment to know when to hand it to Hardware.

Nice to Have

• ROS 2.

• Hardware-in-the-loop rigs and bench automation.

• Fleet telemetry and observability (Grafana, Prometheus, OpenTelemetry).

• Functional safety or comparable standards work.

• On-prem, air-gapped or defence deployment experience.

• Having been on call for hardware in the field.

What We Offer

title: Master Data Engineer
description:
About Vitestro

Founded in 2017 in Utrecht, Vitestro is pioneering the future of blood collection with the Aletta® Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device™ (ARPD™). This groundbreaking medical device combines advanced multi-modal imaging (near-infrared, ultrasound, and Doppler ultrasound) with robotics and AI to perform the entire diagnostic blood draw procedure autonomously.

By addressing critical healthcare staffing shortages and improving patient experience, Vitestro is transforming one of the most common and essential medical procedures. With more than 130 team members and growing rapidly, we are scaling our impact. As we placed our first devices with customers, we are now expanding our team to ensure successful implementation and long-term reliability.

At Vitestro, we are committed to continuous innovation and improvement.

Master Data Engineer

As our Master Data Engineer, you own the accuracy and integrity of the master data behind every Aletta we build: items, bills of materials (BOMs), revisions and routings in our ERP system. You translate the engineering BOM released by R&D into the manufacturing BOM for products, sub-assemblies and spare parts. You also own the change control process between Engineering, Operations and Supply Chain, from the first change request to the verified change in the build. This is a newly created role in our Operations team.

First months at Vitestro

In your first months, your focus will be on two things. First, you set up the change process end to end: from an engineering change to its implementation in the build, including the impact on time and cost. You register changes, organize the impact assessment with Operations, Supply Chain and Quality, chair the change review board, and define effectivity and the disposition of existing stock. Second, you build the manufacturing BOMs for our products from the engineering BOMs. You structure sub-assemblies to match the assembly sequence, add consumables, packaging, labels, kitting and the make/buy split, and set up spare-part and service BOMs together with Service. Along the way, you define how system and module upgrades are managed through the BOM.

You become the single point of contact for master data and change implementation. You make sure every build uses the correct released configuration, so that each Device History Record traces back to the Device Master Record.

This is what success looks like:

After 12 months, engineering changes run through one controlled process, and every change is implemented, verified in the first build and closed in the change record. Product and spare-part BOMs are free of errors, and master data is audit-ready under ISO 13485. Engineering, Operations and Supply Chain know where a change stands and when it reaches the build. Regular comparisons between E-BOM, M-BOM and as-built show no open discrepancies.

You thrive at the intersection of engineering and operations. You are precise and process-minded, you keep the discipline when others are in a hurry, and you are comfortable holding a change that isn't ready yet.

What You’ll Bring:

• A bachelor's or master's background in Mechanical, Mechatronics or Industrial Engineering, or a similar technical field

• 3+ years in master data, BOM, configuration or engineering change management in a manufacturing environment, preferably MedTech or high-tech

• Experience with an ERP system, such as Odoo, SAP or Exact

• Solid understanding of E-BOM and M-BOM structures, item lifecycle and revision control

• Strong ability to align cross-functional stakeholders and keep process discipline

• Comfortable working with detail: analytical, accurate and process-minded

• Excellent communication skills

• Fluent in English

Nice to have:

• Experience in a regulated environment (ISO 13485, DMR/DHR, design transfer)

• Familiarity with a PLM system

• Experience reading technical drawings, and basic 3D CAD knowledge

• Experience with advanced Excel or data tooling for data validation

• Dutch language skills

How We Work

At Vitestro, ownership is not a slogan - it is an expectation. We trust people to take responsibility, make decisions, and drive work forward.

We believe breakthroughs happen when talented people combine dedication, accountability, and teamwork. That means:

• We take initiative rather than wait for direction.

• We focus on execution and delivering results.

• We proactively remove blockers and help each other succeed.

• We challenge ideas, not people.

• We continuously learn, improve, and raise the bar.

• We celebrate team success over individual heroics.

We move fast, but we do so thoughtfully. We care deeply about quality because the technology we build ultimately impacts patients and healthcare professionals.

If you are looking for an environment where you can make a significant contribution, take ownership of meaningful work, and be surrounded by highly motivated colleagues, we'd love to meet you.

What we offer

• Competitive salary including pension plan

• 25 days of annual leave based on a full-time position

• Hybrid work model

• Working together in a high-skilled team with our home base in Utrecht

• Frequent out-of-work activities with our team, and annual company weekend away.

• Training budget

• Opportunity to be key shaper of a new global industry niche: autonomous medical robotics

We’re big fans of working from the office – this is where team spirit comes alive. At the same time, we offer flexibility, allowing up to two (out of 5) days of working from home for those who prefer it.

Are you excited?

We totally understand that and so are we! By joining us, you can play an active role in changing the future of health care. Excited to join our revolution? Then we’d love to hear from you!

If you think you've got what it takes, but you don't meet all the requirements - we still recommend you apply. We would love to learn about your interest and experience and consider if you can be a good fit for Vitestro. Nobody is a perfect fit, and we welcome applications with imperfections. We offer a learning environment where we grow together!

title: Quantitative Researcher - 2027 Graduates
description:
At Graviton, we don't believe the best trading strategies come from following established playbooks. They come from asking better questions. Why does a pattern exist? What is driving it? Is it real or just noise? Can it be explained, modelled and turned into an edge?

As a Quantitative Researcher, you'll work on those questions every day. You'll investigate market behaviour, develop quantitative models, build and test hypotheses and turn insights into trading strategies, working alongside researchers and technologists in an environment where an idea on a whiteboard can reach live trading quickly.

This isn't a role where the answers are in a textbook. The problems are open-ended, the data is enormous, and finding the answers is the job.

Ideal candidates are rigorous thinkers who genuinely enjoy mathematics, programming and figuring out things that aren't obvious, based in our Singapore, London, Amsterdam or US offices.

What You'll Work On

You'll work across quantitative research and systematic trading, taking ideas through the full lifecycle: question, hypothesis, experiment, model, validation, strategy, production. Depending on your team and research interests, your work would include:

• Discovering predictive patterns and sources of alpha from billions of market events

• Formulating hypotheses about market behaviour and designing experiments to test them

• Applying probability, statistics, optimization and machine learning to build predictive models and quantitative signals for systematic trading

• Designing robust backtests and statistical tests to distinguish genuine signals from noise

• Working with large and complex datasets to uncover patterns that aren't immediately visible

• Investigating market microstructure and how markets behave at different timescales

• Evaluating strategy performance, identifying weaknesses and continuously refining models

• Developing research infrastructure and AI-powered tools and agents that make experimentation faster and analysis deeper

• Working closely with technologists to translate research ideas into efficient, production-ready systems

• Exploring new techniques in machine learning, statistics and quantitative finance to uncover new sources of edge

No two research problems are the same. Good research finds patterns. Great research understands why they exist.

What Success Looks Like

Successful researchers at Graviton discover new sources of alpha and turn them into robust trading strategies, build models that hold up under real market conditions and not only in backtests, develop a deep understanding of market behaviour, create research frameworks and tools that make the broader team more effective, work with technologists to take ideas from research into production, and communicate complex quantitative ideas clearly and rigorously. Your impact isn't measured by how many models you build. It's measured by the quality of the ideas you discover and what those ideas enable.

Who We're Looking For

We're looking for exceptional problem solvers who genuinely enjoy mathematics, programming and figuring out things that aren't obvious.

• Degree in a quantitative discipline such as mathematics, physics, computer science, statistics, operations research or machine learning

• No active backlogs

• Strong programming skills in Python and/or C++

• Solid grounding in probability, statistics, linear algebra and optimization, with experience in machine learning, statistical modelling or data analysis, whether through coursework, research or personal projects

• Comfort working with large, complex datasets, and strong analytical thinking

• A passion for applying quantitative thinking and rigorous research to solve open-ended problems in markets

• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex ideas clearly

Prior exposure to quantitative research, algorithmic trading, market microstructure, competitive mathematics or machine learning is valuable, but we care more about how you think than whether you've worked in finance before.

Our Culture

More than specific tools or techniques, we care how you think. We look for people who are curious enough to keep asking why, analytical enough to separate signal from noise, persistent enough to pursue difficult problems, intellectually honest enough to abandon an idea when the evidence says so, and humble enough to keep learning.

At Graviton, researchers sit alongside technologists on specialized trading teams that operate with significant autonomy. You'll have meaningful ownership of research problems from day one: forming your own hypotheses, challenging existing approaches and following the evidence wherever it leads, with the infrastructure and datasets to test ideas at scale, competitive compensation, and a culture where the best idea wins regardless of who proposed it.

Markets are among the most complex systems humans have ever created, and they never stop changing. Neither should our thinking. Every day, someone asks a better question and finds an answer nobody had. That someone could be you.

Want to own how the backend works for everyone, not just one corner of it?

You’ll lead company-level projects like our Auth Service: one authorization layer for PHP and Python, so Python products can handle their traffic directly instead of going through PHP. We're a small team of engineers from core PHP, Infra, and AI backgrounds. We lead technical initiatives across the whole backend and own its health. Product teams build and run their own components, and we give them the tools, standards, and expertise to do it well. Each of us leads our own project, from planning to agreeing with other teams to production. We work in weekly cycles and write our decisions down. Right now we're bringing PHP and Python platform work together into one common backend platform.

• Build the foundations that let new Python products launch and scale without being wired through PHP each time.

• Define clear ownership of technical components across the backend, including who owns monitoring and knowledge for each.

• Find root causes across PHP and Python services using metrics, logs, and distributed tracing.

• Make performance part of everyday work, not something we fix after incidents: clear performance metrics, tools that show where things slow down, and analysis of unusual user behavior that causes degradation.

• Make architecture decisions with high load in mind, working with databases, servers, proxies, and DNS alongside the Infra team.

• Work with the Security team to fix vulnerabilities, build in security practices, and keep libraries and dependencies up to date.

• Improve developer experience: dev environment, CI/CD, routine automation, one documentation approach for PHP and Python, and tools for AI coding assistants.

• Turn product teams' requests into solutions: find what really hurts, propose the best fix, and support them with architecture advice and reviews in shared components.

TO SHINE IN THIS ROLE 💥

You'll need:

• Production backend experience in PHP or Python, and the ability to read and work with the other. You'll write production code in both.

• Experience with high-load production systems and improving their performance.

• Experience designing multi-component systems with clear boundaries, planning for failures, rollout, and rollback, with security in mind.

• Experience comparing technical options, naming the trade-offs, and explaining your choice in writing (ADRs, Design Docs).

• Hands-on observability experience: metrics, dashboards, alerts, logs, and distributed tracing, and using them to find root causes.

• Experience leading a project that spans several teams: breaking it into small, testable steps, getting other teams on board, and taking it to production.

• A track record of improving engineering quality beyond your own tasks, for example setting up error monitoring, or a new process when things kept breaking.

• Enough infrastructure knowledge (databases, servers, proxies, DNS) to work well with Infra and see how your changes affect them.

It would be great if you have:

• Experience on a Platform or Core team.

• Strong production experience in both PHP and Python.

• Experience with authentication and authorization systems (for example, JWT or Ory Oathkeeper).

• Experience defining SLOs and building symptom-based alerts.

Binnen onze Smart Devices afdeling bouwen we apps die impact maken. Van media apps voor bedrijven als Pathé en de NPO met miljoenen gebruikers, tot de app van het KNMI waarmee we belangrijke weerswaarschuwingen zoals code rood meldingen afgeven. We maken geen compromissen op kwaliteit en zoeken altijd naar de best mogelijke oplossing, tot in de kleinste details.

Om onze groeiambities te realiseren zoeken we een Backend Software Developer. Iemand die energie krijgt van het ontwikkelen van sterke backend-omgevingen, het schrijven van strakke code en het operationeel krijgen én houden van de onderliggende cloud-infrastructuur voor applicaties met miljoenen gebruikers.

Als Backend Software Developer ben je een onmisbare schakel in de backend-trajecten van onze applicaties. Je bouwt de schaalbare, onzichtbare motor achter hoogwaardige innovaties en zorgt dat onze infrastructuur robuust staat. Je bent analytisch sterk en je krijgt er energie van om technische requirements te vertalen naar logische cloud-infrastructuren die je vervolgens zélf bouwt. Je werkt nauw samen met onze multidisciplinaire ontwikkelteams en zorgt dat de code soepel draait. Geen haastwerk, maar engineering met diepgang en visie.

Wat je zal gaan doen:

• Ontwikkelen en operationeel maken van serverless backends en event-driven API's met TypeScript (AWS Lambda / Serverless Functions).

• Zelfstandig opzetten van cloud-infrastructuren met behulp van Infrastructure as Code (bijv. via AWS CDK, Terraform of CloudFormation).

We zoeken een developer met een HBO werk- en denkniveau die al de nodige stappen heeft gezet in het bouwen van cloud-native applicaties. Je hebt sterke ervaring met de TypeScript/Node.js stack en modern software-development zoals Agile/Scrum, CI/CD en Infrastructure as Code kent voor jou geen geheimen.

We bouwen niet voor de massa, maar voor betekenis. Onze klanten komen uit sectoren die er écht toe doen – van zorg en educatie tot duurzaamheid en publieke dienstverlening. title: Interim Senior Community Manager
description:
Who we are

We believe travel can create Citizens of the World. When people cross Europe slowly, by train, they come back more curious, more open and better able to understand people unlike themselves.

With colleagues from more than 50 countries, our diversity sparks curiosity, insight and a culture of openness, which is essential to understanding our travellers and one another.

Three values connect everyone at Interrail: we lead with our purpose, we own our impact, and we choose for growth.

We work in a hybrid way, from our office in Utrecht and our homes across the Netherlands.

We’re on the search for...

Someone who has built a community for a brand before, and who can bring ours to life online and offline. Since 1959, Interrail has been more than a rail pass. We’re now building it into a cultural movement, and our community is where that movement becomes real: the deeper you travel through Europe, the more the journey changes you, told by the people who lived it.

In 2027 our community moves into the Interrail app and website. Our product and technical team builds the platform. You make it a community: you shape the community vision, bring the first members in, and create the moments, online and in real life, that make travellers come back and help each other.

The Brand team shapes what Interrail stands for and how it shows up wherever travellers meet us. We own our brand platform and positioning, and our community, bringing The Interrail Effect to life through the people who’ve travelled with us. We work closely with Product, Social & Community, Creative & Content, CRM, and the PR & Partnerships teams to keep every touchpoint consistent and culturally sharp.

This is a nine-month interim contract. The team meets in the office a minimum of twice per week, so you’ll be required to join those days to work alongside your colleagues.

What you’ll be doing

You’ll be part of the Brand team, reporting to the Brand Lead who owns the Community Program. You’ll lead the community from launch to a community that’s live, safe, well populated and growing, online and offline.

The community isn’t a loyalty scheme or a fan club. It’s where travellers tell the truth about their journeys, inspire others and help the next person go and experience it. You’ll work closely with Product (Social Connection and Loyalty team), Customer Experience, Legal and Privacy, PR & Partnerships, Social, and our Creator Partnerships and Creative colleagues.

You’ll be:

• Shaping the community vision, values and member code with the Brand Lead, and laying the foundations for Interrail as a cultural movement, online and offline.

• Building the community strategy: who we bring in first, which journeys launch first and how the community grows after launch.

• Bringing our existing members across as founding voices, and working with Content and Marketing to onboard our Pioneers.

• Launching the first community rituals, and making the community a source of real traveller stories for the brand.

• Designing and running a first pilot of real-world moments, such as gatherings at stations or partner places, with PR & Partnerships and Social.

• Building good relationships with the independent Interrail communities on Facebook, Reddit and beyond. We partner with them; we never try to replace them.

• Keeping the community safe: setting guidelines, the moderation approach with Customer Experience, and working with Legal, Privacy, and Safety so nothing goes live until it’s signed off.

• Being the members’ voice in our Product team, measuring community health with Analytics and CRM, and creating a playbook so what you build lasts.

What we’re looking for

Here’s what will help you in this role. If you don’t match every point, we’d still love to hear from you.

• 8+ years building communities for brands, including at least one you grew from launch.

• Experience running community both online and in real life, such as events, meet-ups or ambassador programs.

• You have written a community vision or strategy and turned it into a plan that others follow.

• A track record of building early momentum, so people join and champion the community, not just follow it.

• Experience setting moderation and safety policies, and comfort working with Legal and Privacy on consent, safeguarding and GDPR.

• A clear point of view on what makes a community healthy, and the confidence to defend it with product teams.

• Organised, good at documenting and comfortable working across many teams, so what you build outlasts your contract.

• A genuine interest in train travel, meeting locals, new experiences and other cultures.

Bonus points for experience with community platforms or social SDKs, multilingual moderation, or a long rail trip through Europe of your own.

Curious to apply?

Apply directly through our careers page.

• We’ll ask you to share your CV in English (our business language) and tell us why you’re interested in Interrail and this role. It doesn’t hurt to be creative; we enjoy seeing your personality shine through.

• For some roles, we may also ask you to complete a short task based on the real job, so you can show us your skills in practice.

If we’d like to get to know you better, the next step is a first conversation with Talent Acquisition, followed by interviews with the team. It’s a two-way conversation: a chance for you to explore Interrail, and for us to get to know you.

To keep our hiring fair, we use blind screening in the early stages. Your name, photo, date of birth, gender, nationality, contact details and social media links are hidden, so our first decisions are based only on your skills, experience and potential.

In the meantime

If you’re curious, why not check us out on LinkedIn and get a sense of our culture and values?

Got questions? Our team would be happy to help: just drop us a note at www.interrail.com.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Customs
description:
About Flexport: 

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year. 

The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

Why Customs Matters More Than Ever

International trade is under more pressure than ever before. With tariffs, shifting regulations, and geopolitical uncertainty, customs has gone from a back-office function to a boardroom priority. The recent trade crisis—sparked by Trump-era tariffs—has made customs the single most complex challenge for global businesses. For many, it’s the difference between keeping supply chains moving or grinding them to a halt.

That’s where we come in. The Customs Technology team at Flexport is leading the charge. We are building the systems that help entrepreneurs and global brands navigate complexity, stay compliant, and keep the world’s goods flowing.

The opportunity: 

Customs brokerage is one of the largest, most under-innovated opportunities in logistics. Legacy customs brokers are stuck with outdated systems and manual processes—they simply can’t adapt fast enough.

Flexport is growing fast because we’re different. We are the only big tech company in the space, and the only freight forwarder that got founded after the launch of Netscape. Being a tech company, we can move much faster than our competitors, and give our customers the service they expect in this day and age. We can deploy things like LLM agents at scale, in an industry that is ripe to be disrupted by this technology.

Things we ❤️

• Leveraging AI in a safe way to eliminate mundane work for customs brokers and automate customs every step of the way

• Modeling complex and ambiguous domains into fully automated workflows

• Building highly performant and reliable Kotlin services on our cutting-edge infrastructure platform

• Collaborating with end users across the globe to create the best possible product: removing toil and surfacing interesting cases

You will:

• Work closely with business partners and product managers to distill complex business problems into elegant technical solutions.

• Work on systems that represent the real-world intricacies of logistics entities and the process of moving cargo in and out of countries.

• Build and launch products rapidly and incrementally. We ship to production dozens of times per day.

• Geek out about shipping, customs regulations and logistics. (We do this often.)

• Figure out the most efficient way for our customers and partners to participate in the process of moving freight across borders.

• Design and build deep, complex integrations with government agencies and partners.

• Automate archaic customs filing processes and save the operations team thousands of phone calls per week.

• Deliver supply chain insights to logistics teams via a world-class analytics experience.

• Create beautiful and efficient domain models for the incredibly complex world of freight forwarding.

You should have:

• ≥ 5 years of experience writing software, and a strong engineering background.

• A love of simple, well-tested code that is easy to extend and hard to break.

• The ability to convey technical ideas in common terms to business partners, product managers, designers and engineers alike.

• A bias for action. When you see a problem, you solve it.

• A desire to develop your tooling repertoire. We are tech-agnostic regarding candidate background, but our platform is built with Ruby.

• Non-optional: an aptitude for learning quickly.

How we work:

• We come to the office at two to three times a week to hang out, have lunch, white board, and collaborate

• We have the latest and greatest hardware and software for you to work with

• We’re agile, but not married to a single doctrine like scrum. The teams decide how they work best.

• Stack: we’re coming from a React/Flow + Ruby on Rails monolith, and moving to React/Typescript, Kotlin Microservices on Kubernetes. We also use and love GraphQL, GRPC, Postgres, Kafka and Snowflake

What's in it for you?

• An opportunity to contribute to one of the fastest-growing companies, where you’ll have the chance to create a global impact while being a part of a  thriving multinational environment 

• Daily catered lunches incl. vegetarian options, breakfast, snacks and soft drinks available in our office on daily basis 

• Commute expenses: Flexport will cover  home-office commuting costs for employees living outside of Amsterdam

• 25 working days as vacation days based on full time employment.

• Health insurance: Flexport offers a collective health insurance plan including a basic package and any available additional packages. Your monthly premium is fully paid by Flexport.

• Equity program: every team member becomes a shareholder, aligning our success with yours. As a private company in a multi-trillion dollar industry, you have a direct stake in our collective growth and success.

• Employee Assistance Program through Aetna Resources for Living: Flexport provides an employer-sponsored program at no cost to you and your household members

• Parental leave benefit: Flexport is here to support you and your families in one of the most important times in life – the birth of a child! Our parental leave program allows both mothers and partners to take time off from work for pregnancy, childbirth, and to bond with your new child.
